title: Beans on Toast with Cheese
subtitle: baked beans on thick toast with melted cheddar
excerpt: Beans on toast with cheese is thick slices of toast loaded with hot baked beans and a generous layer of grated cheddar. The cheese goes on top of the hot beans rather than under the grill, so it melts from the heat of the beans rather than browning. Ready in five minutes from cold.
sourceNotes: Baked beans on toast became a British standard in the first half of the twentieth century after  began producing tinned beans in tomato sauce in the UK in the 1920s. The cheese addition is a common British home variation.

content.text: Beans on toast with cheese is exactly what it sounds like: tinned baked beans heated through, spooned over thick toast, and finished with grated cheddar that melts on contact with the hot beans. It is one of the fastest hot meals in any British kitchen and satisfying in a way that needs no explaining.
Heat the beans and toast the bread
Tip {{baked-beans}} of baked beans into a small saucepan. Heat over a medium heat, stirring occasionally, for 3 to 4 minutes until hot through. Meanwhile, toast the bread to your preferred shade.

Butter the toast if you like, then place two slices on each plate. Spoon the hot beans over the toast and immediately scatter {{cheddar}} of grated cheddar on top. The heat from the beans will melt the cheese in about 30 seconds. Grind over a little black pepper if you like.

items.symptom: The beans are sticking to the pan
items.cause: The heat is too high and the tomato sauce is catching on the bottom.
items.fix: Use a medium heat and stir every minute. Baked beans need gentle, patient heating rather than a high blast.

items.cause: The beans were not hot enough when the cheese was added, or the cheese was too cold from the fridge.
items.fix: Make sure the beans are steaming hot when you spoon them over, and use cheese at room temperature. If it still will not melt, briefly place the plate under a hot grill for 30 seconds.

content.text: Baked beans on toast is a British dish that has no real equivalent elsewhere. In the US, baked beans are a barbecue side; in the UK, they are a meal in their own right, eaten at breakfast, lunch, or as a late-night snack. The cheese version is a natural British upgrade: cheddar on everything. Adding Worcestershire sauce and a dash of Tabasco to the beans is another common variant. The dish is equally good with brown bread.
